label: rem:quenched
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:quenched}
As mentioned
in~\cite[Sec.~2]{KestenSidoraviciusVares2022}, the event $\{\xi : \mathbb{P}(C_{0}\text{ is infinite}\mid\xi)>0\}$ is a tail event of
the i.i.d.\ sequence $\xi$, so that~\eqref{eq:quenched} follows from
$\Theta(p_{G},p_{c},\delta)>0$ by Kolmogorov's zero--one law. Therefore, it suffices to prove the first assertion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

label: prop:speeds
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:speeds}
For every $\delta\in[0,1]$, there exists $\alpha(\delta)\in[-\infty,1]$ such that
\[
  \frac{r_{n}}{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\alpha(\delta)
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \frac{\ell_{n}}{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}-\alpha(\delta)
\]
almost surely under $\mathbb{P}$.

name: Existence of the edge speeds

title: Proof

label: prop:strict
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Positivity of the edge speeds

label: lem:basic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:basic}
Let $\xi$ be an environment, let $m\le n$, and let $A\subseteq H_{m}$ be
infinite and not bounded from below. Then $\mathbb{P}^{\xi}(\zeta_{m,n}(A)=\emptyset)=0$
and, for every integer $k\ge0$ and every $b\in H_{m}$,
\[
  \mathbb{P}^{\xi}\bigl(\max\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})\le b-2k\bigr)
  \ \le\ \bigl(1-p_{c}^{\,n-m}\bigr)^{k}.
\]
In particular, $\mathbb{E}^{\xi}|\max\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})|<\infty$ and $\mathbb{E}^{\xi}|r_{n}|<\infty$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $x\in H_{m}$, let $D(x):=\{(x+i,m+i):1\le i\le n-m\}$ be the ascending
diagonal issued from $(x,m)$. Diagonals issued from distinct points are disjoint and each is
entirely open with probability at least $p_{c}^{\,n-m}$ because
$p_{\xi_{i}}\gep_{c}$. If $x\in A$ and $D(x)$ is open then
$x+(n-m)\in\zeta_{m,n}(A)$.

Since $A$ is infinite and not bounded from below, we may pick
$x_{0}>x_{1}>\dots$ in $A$. The diagonals $D(x_{0}),D(x_{1}),\dots$ being
disjoint, the corresponding events are conditionally independent given $\xi$, so
that the probability that none of $D(x_{0}),\dots,D(x_{j-1})$ is open is at most
$(1-p_{c}^{\,n-m})^{j}$. Letting $j\to\infty$ shows that
$\zeta_{m,n}(A)\ne\emptyset$ almost surely.

The same argument applied to the $k$ points $b,b-2,\dots,b-2(k-1)$ of
$H_{m}^{b}$ gives that if $D(b-2i)$ is open for some
$0\le i\le k-1$, then $b-2i+(n-m)\in\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})$, thus
\[
  \max\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})\ \ge\ b-2(k-1)+(n-m)\ >\ b-2k ,
\]
so that the event $\{\max\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})\le b-2k\}$ forces all $k$
diagonals to be closed.

Finally, $\max\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})\le b+(n-m)$, since the $x$-coordinate increases
by at most $1$ at each step, and the above bound gives an exponential tail on
the left, thus $\mathbb{E}^{\xi}|\max\zeta_{m,n}(H_{m}^{b})|<\infty$, uniformly in $\xi$.
head: environment

label: lem:gain
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gain}
Let $\xi$ be an environment, let $m\le n$, and let $A\subseteq B\subseteq H_{m}$
with $A$ infinite and not bounded from below and such that
$x^{*}:=\max B<\infty$ satisfies $x^{*}>\max A$. Then
\[
  \mathbb{E}^{\xi}\bigl[\max\zeta_{m,n}(B)-\max\zeta_{m,n}(A)\bigr]\ \ge\ 2 .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: lem:line
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:line}
For every $1\le m\le n$ and every $\delta\in[0,1]$,
\[
\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{m}r_{n}]\ge2(p_{G}-p_{c}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $q:=1-\delta$ for the density of good lines and see $a_{n}$ as a
function of $q$. The edge $r_{n}$ depends on the environment only through
$(\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n})$, so for $w\in\{0,1\}^{n}$ we write
$\mathbb{E}^{\xi}[r_{n}]=\mathbb{E}^{w}[r_{n}]$ whenever $\xi$ agrees with $w$ on the first $n$
lines. Let $\mu_{q}$ be the law of a single line, $\mu_{q}(0)=q$ and
$\mu_{q}(1)=1-q$, so that
\[
  a_{n}=\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{n}}\ \prod_{i=1}^{n}\mu_{q}(w_{i})\ \mathbb{E}^{w}[r_{n}].
\]
This is a polynomial in $q$. Indeed, the sum is finite, and the coefficients
$\mathbb{E}^{w}[r_{n}]$ are finite by Lemma~\ref{lem:basic} and do not depend on $q$.
Since $\mathrm{d}\mu_{q}(0)/\mathrm{d}q=1$ and
$\mathrm{d}\mu_{q}(1)/\mathrm{d}q=-1$, the product rule gives
\[
  \frac{\mathrm{d}a_{n}}{\mathrm{d}q}
  =\sum_{m=1}^{n}\ \sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{n}}
    \varepsilon(w_{m})\prod_{i\ne m}\mu_{q}(w_{i})\ \mathbb{E}^{w}[r_{n}],
  \qquad \varepsilon(0)=1,\ \varepsilon(1)=-1 .
\]
For fixed $m$, the weight $\prod_{i\ne m}\mu_{q}(w_{i})$ does not depend on
$w_{m}$. It only involves the status of the lines other than $H_{m}$. Pairing
each environment $w$ with the one obtained by changing the status of $H_{m}$,
and using $\varepsilon(0)=1$, $\varepsilon(1)=-1$, the inner sum becomes
\[
  \sum_{v}\ \prod_{i\ne m}\mu_{q}(v_{i})
  \Bigl(\mathbb{E}^{\xi^{m,G}}[r_{n}]-\mathbb{E}^{\xi^{m,B}}[r_{n}]\Bigr),
\]
where $v$ runs over the $2^{n-1}$ environments of the lines
$H_{i}$, $i\le n$, $i\ne m$, and $\xi$ is any environment agreeing with $v$ off
$m$. Since $\xi^{m,G}$ and $\xi^{m,B}$ do not depend on $\xi_{m}$, this is
exactly $\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{m}r_{n}]$. Notice that we recover Russo's formula. Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:line} gives
\[
  \frac{\mathrm{d}a_{n}}{\mathrm{d}q}
  =\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Delta_{m}r_{n}\bigr]
  \ \ge\ 2\,(p_{G}-p_{c})\,n
  \qquad\text{for every } q\in[0,1].
\]
It remains to determine the constant of integration. At $q=0$ every line is bad,
so that $a_{n}=\mathbb{E}_{p_{c}}[r_{n}]$, the homogeneous critical model, whose edge
speed vanishes, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}_{p_{c}}[r_{n}]/n=0$,
by the classical result of Durrett and Griffeath~\cite{DurrettGriffeath1983}. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:speeds} this limit is also an infimum, so that
$\mathbb{E}_{p_{c}}[r_{n}]\ge0$ for every $n\ge1$. Integrating therefore gives
$a_{n}\ge2(p_{G}-p_{c})\,q\,n$ for every $n\ge1$, and taking the infimum over $n$
gives~\eqref{eq:strict}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The factor 2 in the lower bound of $\alpha(\delta)$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:strict} may be surprising since $\alpha(\delta) \leq 1$, but it is in fact not a contradiction. In the classical homogeneous oriented percolation model on $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}$, there are exactly $2^n$ oriented paths of length $n$ issued from a given site and the $n$ sites of a given path are distinct and independently open with probability $p$. Therefore, $\mathbb{P}_p(\exists$ an open oriented path of length $n$ from the origin$)\le (2p)^n$, so that $p_{c}\ge 1/2$. Hence, $2(p_{G}-p_{c})\le 1$, and~\eqref{eq:strict} is consistent with
$\alpha(\delta)\le 1$.
head: environment

label: rem:why-critical
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:why-critical}
In Sections~\ref{sec:speeds} and~\ref{sec:strict}, the criticality of the bad lines is used only through the constant of
integration. Indeed, Lemmas~\ref{lem:basic},~\ref{lem:gain} and~\ref{lem:line}
use the standing assumption $p_{B}=p_{c}$, $p_{G}>p_{c}$ only through $p_{\xi_{i}}\ge p_{B}>0$: replacing $p_{c}$
by an arbitrary $p_{B}\in(0,p_{G})$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:basic}, and the
event of Lemma~\ref{lem:line} by $\{p_{B}\le U_{v}<p_{G}\}$, the same argument
gives
\[
  \frac{\mathrm{d}a_{n}}{\mathrm{d}q}\ \ge\ 2\,(p_{G}-p_{B})\,n
  \qquad\text{and hence}\qquad
  \alpha(\delta)\ \ge\ \alpha_{\mathrm{hom}}(p_{B})+2\,(p_{G}-p_{B})(1-\delta),
\]
where $\alpha_{\mathrm{hom}}(p)$ denotes the right edge speed of the
homogeneous model with parameter $p$. Proposition~\ref{prop:strict} is the case
$p_{B}=p_{c}$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm{hom}}(p_{c})=0$ by~\cite{DurrettGriffeath1983}.

For $p_{B}<p_{c}$, $\alpha_{\mathrm{hom}}(p_{B})=-\infty$ (see~\cite[Sec.~7]{Durrett1984}) and the estimate is trivial for every
$\delta<1$. This is why percolation for $p_{B}<p_{c}$ and $\delta$ small
in~\cite{KestenSidoraviciusVares2022} requires different arguments. In this sense,
$p_{c}$ is the smallest value of $p_{B}$ for which the present arguments say
something, and the only one for which the conclusion is not already trivial,
since for $p_{B}>p_{c}$ percolation holds even at $\delta=1$.

label: prop:boxsuper
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:boxsuper}
For every $\rho>0$ and
every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $n_{0}$ such that, for every $n\ge n_{0}$,
letting
\[
  u=(\rho n,0),
  \qquad
  v^{+}=(\alpha n,n),
  \qquad
  v^{-}=(-\alpha n,n),
\]
we have
\[
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(C^{\uparrow}(R(u,v^{+}))\bigr)>1-\varepsilon
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(C^{\uparrow}(R(u,v^{-}))\bigr)>1-\varepsilon.
\]
head: environment
name: Supercritical box-crossing

label: lem:tail
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The reflection $(x,n)\mapsto(-x,n)$ preserves $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}$ together with its oriented
graph structure, it preserves $\mathbb{P}$ and maps $R(u,v^{+})$ onto a
translate of $R(u,v^{-})$. Therefore, the second inequality follows from the first one.

By the convention of Section~\ref{sec:geometry}, it suffices to consider $R:=(-\rho n/2,0)+R(u,v^{+})$. Note that $\rho n\ge2$ for $n$ large, so that the lowest and highest lines of $R$
contain at least one site and $C^{\uparrow}(R)$ cannot be empty.
Consider the event
\[
  A_{n}:=\Bigl\{\,\alpha m-\frac{\rho}{4}n\ \le\ r_{m}\ \le\ \alpha m+\frac{\rho}{4}n
    \quad\text{for every } m\le n-1\,\Bigr\}.
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:speeds}, $r_{m}/m\to\alpha$ almost surely, hence
$\mathbb{P}(A_{n})\to1$ as $n\to\infty$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:basic} applied to $H_{0}^{-}$, the set $\zeta_{n-1}(H_{0}^{-})$
is almost surely non-empty. Thus, there is an open path
$\gamma=((x_{0},0),\dots,(x_{n-1},n-1))$ with $x_{0}\in H_{0}^{-}$ and $x_{n-1}=r_{n-1}$.
If multiple such paths exist, we choose one using some arbitrary procedure. On $A_{n}$, since $x_{i}\in\zeta_{i}(H_{0}^{-})$ for every $i$, we have $x_{i}\le r_{i}\le\alpha i+\rho n/4$, so that $\gamma$ never exits $R$ through its right side. Its endpoint $x_{n-1}=r_{n-1}$ satisfies $\alpha(n-1)-\rho n/4\le x_{n-1}\le\alpha(n-1)+\rho n/4$, so that it belongs to the top side of $R$. Notice that, in contrast with
the proof of~\cite[Lemma~8]{ArcherEtAl2026}, we do not need to treat heights of different parities separately, since the bound holds at every height rather than at even ones only.

It remains to exclude the case where $\gamma$ exits $R$ through its left side (or starts to the left of the bottom side of $R$). Suppose that it does, and let $0 \leq i< n-1$ be the first height at which $x_{i}<\alpha i-\rho n/2$. Since $\gamma$ ends at
$x_{n-1}\ge\alpha(n-1)-\rho n/4$, the portion of $\gamma$ above height $i$ is an
open path from $(x_{i},i)$ to height $n-1$ reaching an $x$-coordinate at least
$\alpha(n-1)-\rho n/4$, so that
\[
  \max\zeta_{i,n-1}\bigl(H_{i}^{\,b_{i}}\bigr)
  \ \ge\ \alpha(n-1)-\frac{\rho}{4}n,
  \qquad
  b_{i}:=\max\Bigl\{x\in H_{i}:x<\alpha i-\frac{\rho}{2}n\Bigr\}.
\]
Since $b_{i}<\alpha i-\rho n/2$, we deduce
\[
  \max\zeta_{i,n-1}\bigl(H_{i}^{\,b_{i}}\bigr)
  \ >\ b_{i}+\alpha(n-1-i)+\frac{\rho}{4}n.
\]
Each $b_{i}$ being deterministic, Lemma~\ref{lem:tail}, applied with $m=n-1$
and $\rho/4$ in place of $\rho$, and a union bound over $0\le i<n-1$ bound by
$n\,e^{-cn}$ the probability that, on $A_{n}$, $\gamma$ exits $R$ through its
left side. Hence, on $A_{n}$ minus an event of probability at most
$n\,e^{-cn}$, the path $\gamma$ stays in $R$ and crosses it from the base to the
top, so that $\mathbb{P}(C^{\uparrow}(R))\ge\mathbb{P}(A_{n})-n\,e^{-cn}>1-\varepsilon$ for
$n$ large enough.
head: environment

label: thm:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018}
There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$ large enough, there exists
$w_{n} \in [\varepsilon n^{2/5},n^{1-\varepsilon}]\cap\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
  \mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(C^{\rightarrow}(R(3u,v))\bigr)\ \ge\ \varepsilon,
  \qquad
  \mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(C^{\uparrow}(R(u,3v))\bigr)\ \ge\ \varepsilon,
  \qquad
  \mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(C^{\leftarrow}(R(3u,v))\bigr)\ \ge\ \varepsilon,
\]
with $u=(w_{n},0)$ and $v=(0,n)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Notice that the boxes above are rectangular, while those of
Proposition~\ref{prop:boxsuper} are tilted along the directions
$(\pm\alpha(\delta),1)$. For the classical oriented site percolation model at $p_{c}$, the edge
speed is $0$, so the process has no drift and we should not tilt the boxes.

Since $w_{n}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}$, the width of such a rectangular box grows strictly slower than its length. Unlike in the non-oriented case, the natural box at
$p_{c}$ is not $n\times n$ but $w_{n}\times n$, $w_{n}$ being
comparable to the typical width of a critical cluster reaching height $n$~\cite[Proposition~4.1(iii)]{DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018}.
head: environment

label: cor:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018quenched
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018quenched}
With $\varepsilon$, $n$, $w_n$, $u$ and $v$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018}, the
three lower bounds hold with $\mathbb{P}^{\xi}$ in place of $\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}$, for every
environment $\xi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The three crossing events are increasing in the occupation configuration
$(\eta_{z})$, and $\eta^{\mathrm{crit}}$, which has law $\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}$, satisfies
$\eta^{\mathrm{crit}}\le\eta^{\xi}$ by~\eqref{eq:sandwich}. Any crossing realized
by $\eta^{\mathrm{crit}}$ is therefore realized by $\eta^{\xi}$, uniformly
in $\xi$.
head: environment

label: lem:planar
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At the same height, two sites are at an even distance, so $\gamma_1-\gamma_2$ takes
even values and since both $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ change their
$x$-coordinate by $\pm1$ at each step, $\gamma_1-\gamma_2$ changes by
$0$ or $\pm2$ between consecutive heights. Since $h'$ belongs to the set defining $s$, we have $h\le s\le h'$. If
$s=h$, then $\gamma_1(h)-\gamma_2(h)$ is both non-positive and non-negative,
hence zero. Otherwise $\gamma_1-\gamma_2$ is negative, hence at most $-2$, at
$s-1$ by definition of $s$, and non-negative at $s$. Since it changes
by at most $2$, it vanishes at $s$. The last assertion of (i) is trivial. For (ii), if $\pi$ shared a site with neither $\gamma_1$ nor $\gamma_2$ on
$(h,h']$, then $\gamma_1-\pi$ and $\pi-\gamma_2$ would never vanish and therefore would be strictly negative on
$(h,h']$. Thus, $\gamma_1-\pi + \pi-\gamma_2 = \gamma_1-\gamma_2$ would also be negative on $(h,h']$, contradicting
$\gamma_1(h')=\gamma_2(h')$.
head: environment

label: thm:HilarioSaSanchisTeixeira2026
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:HilarioSaSanchisTeixeira2026}
Let $p,\theta\in(0,1)$ and
$\mathbb{V}:=\{(i,n)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}_{+}:i+n\ \text{even}\}$, with the two oriented
edges $\bigl((i,n),(i\pm1,n+1)\bigr)$ issued from each vertex, the second
coordinate playing the role of time. Let $\zeta=(\zeta_{n})_{n\ge0}$ be a
sequence of i.i.d.\ random variables with $\mathbb{P}(\zeta_{n}=k)=(1-\theta)\theta^{k}$
for $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Conditionally on $\zeta$, declare each of the two edges issued
from $(i,n)$ to be open independently with probability $p^{1+\zeta_{n}}$, and
denote by $\mathbb{P}^{\zeta}_{p}$ the law of this process. There exists $c>0$
such that if $\theta\le c$ and $p\ge1-c$, then for almost every $\zeta$, under
$\mathbb{P}^{\zeta}_{p}$, there is an infinite open path starting at $(0,0)$
with positive probability.

label: def:renorm
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Open vertices and edges

label: prop:reconstruction
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Reconstruction of an infinite open path

label: lem:ladderpath
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ladderpath}
Let $N=2k+1\ge3$ be odd and let $z\in\mathbb{R}\times[0,\infty)$. On the event
$\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(z))$ there is an open path $\Gamma$ contained in
$\Lambda_{N}(z)$, from a site at its lowest height to a site at its highest height,
these being $\lceil z_{2}\rceil$ and $\lceil z_{2}\rceil+6LN-1$. In particular
$C^{\uparrow}(z+R((3w,0),(0,6LN)))$ occurs.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The construction is purely geometric, so it holds at any position and we take
$z=0$. For $k=1$ there is nothing to prove, so assume $k\ge2$.

On the event $\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(0))$, choose once and for all, by an
arbitrary procedure, a crossing path $\gamma_{j}$ of each $T_{j}$,
$0\le j\le k-1$, and a crossing path $\sigma_{j}$ of each $W_{j}$,
$0\le j\le k-2$. Fix $j\le k-2$, and denote by $a$ and $b$ the heights of the two
ends of $\sigma_{j}$. Both $\gamma_{j}$ and $\gamma_{j+1}$ are defined at
every height of $W_{j}$, these being the top $6L$ lines of $T_{j}$ and the bottom
$6L$ lines of $T_{j+1}$, thus they are in particular defined on $[a,b]$.

Suppose $j$ is even, so that $T_{j}$ occupies the columns $[0,w)$ and $T_{j+1}$
the columns $[2w,3w)$, while $W_{j}$ occupies $[0,3w)$. Being an open path of
$\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}$, $\sigma_j$ moves by $\pm1$ at each height, so it takes every integer value
between $\sigma_j(a) \in \{0,1\}$ and $\sigma_j(b) \in \{3w-2,3w-1\}$, depending
on the parity of the height. In particular the heights
\[
    s_{1}:=\min\{h\in[a,b]:\sigma_j(h)=w\},
  \qquad
  s_{2}:=\min\{h\in[a,b]:\sigma_j(h)=2w\}
\]
are well defined, and $s_{1}<s_{2}$ since $\sigma_j$ reaches $2w$ only after
reaching $w$. By construction, the rectangular boxes $W_{j}$ and $T_{j}$ have the same
leftmost column and the rectangular boxes $W_{j}$ and $T_{j+1}$ the same rightmost one,
thus
\[
  \sigma_j(a)\le\gamma_{j}(a),
  \qquad
    \sigma_j(s_{1})=w\ge\gamma_{j}(s_{1}),
\]
\[
  \sigma_j(s_{2})=2w\le\gamma_{j+1}(s_{2}),
  \qquad
  \sigma_j(b)\ge\gamma_{j+1}(b).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:planar}(i), applied on $[a,s_{1}]$ to $\sigma_j$ and
$\gamma_{j}$, then on $[s_{2},b]$ to $\sigma_j$ and $\gamma_{j+1}$, gives
heights $s\in[a,s_{1}]$ and $s'\in[s_{2},b]$ with
$\sigma_j(s)=\gamma_{j}(s)$ and $\sigma_j(s')=\gamma_{j+1}(s')$. As
$s\le s_{1}<s_{2}\le s'$, following $\gamma_{j}$ up to the height
$s$, then $\sigma_j$ up to the height $s'$, then $\gamma_{j+1}$, gives an
open path contained in $T_{j}\cup W_{j}\cup T_{j+1}$ which crosses it from the
bottom line of $T_{j}$ to the top line of $T_{j+1}$. If $j$ is odd, the same
argument applies in the opposite direction. Iterating on $0 \le j \le k-2$ gives
$\Gamma$.

By~\eqref{eq:Tj} and~\eqref{eq:Wj} the rails occupy the columns $[0,w)$ or
$[2w,3w)$ and the rungs the columns $[0,3w)$, so that
$\Lambda_{N}(z)\subseteq z+R((3w,0),(0,6LN))$, both sets having the same lowest
and highest lines. The last assertion follows.

title: Proposition

\label{prop:renormperc}
For $L$ large enough, depending on $\delta$ only, there is a sequence
$(X_{k})_{k\ge0}$ of $\{0,1\}$-valued random variables such that the scheme
associated with $(X_{k})_{k\ge0}$ as in Section~\ref{sec:renormlattice}

\]

body_md:
As in Section~\ref{sec:geometry} for a box, for a region $A\subseteq\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}$ and a height $h$ we write $A_{h}$ for the set of $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that $(x,h)\in A$, and, for a set $I$ of heights, $A_{I}:=\bigcup_{h\in I}A_{h}$, the $x$-coordinates of the

label: lem:regions
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Throughout we use $10\beta-2<g\le10\beta$, which follows from~\eqref{eq:g}, and
$2\beta\ge3w+4\ge10$, which follows from~\eqref{eq:wsmall} and $w\ge2$.

\emph{Point (i).}
By~\eqref{eq:corridor}, $D_{i,n}$ is contained in
$(ig-\beta,ig+\beta)\times[h_{n},\tilde h_{n}+6L)$,
that is in the slabs $\tau_{n-1}+1,\dots,\tau_{n}$ by~\eqref{eq:heights}. At the same floor, the indices of two vertices of $\mathbb{V}$ differ by at least $2$, hence their columns by at least $2g>2\beta$, so that the rectangles above are disjoint. Two
corridors at floors $n<l$ occupy disjoint sets of slabs, since
$\tau_{n}\le\tau_{l-1}<\tau_{l-1}+1$.

\emph{Point (ii).}  Using the symmetry of our construction, we only prove the assertion for $E^{+}_{i,n}$.
The heights of $E^{+}_{i,n}$ are, by~\eqref{eq:transport} and
\eqref{eq:transportflat}, those of $[\tilde h_{n},\tilde h_{n}+18L)$, that is
those of the slab $\tau_{n}$ together with the bottom $6L$ lines of the slab
$\tau_{n}+1$, while $D_{j,l}$ occupies the slabs $\tau_{l-1}+1,\dots,\tau_{l}$,
so only $l\in\{n,n+1\}$ can occur. Since
\[
  \bigl(B^{+}_{i,n}\bigr)_{[\tilde h_{n},\tilde h_{n}+12L)}
  \subseteq[ig-5\beta,ig+9\beta),
  \qquad
  \bigl(B^{-,t}_{i,n}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}\subseteq(ig-3\beta,ig+5\beta),
\]
the set $E^{+}_{i,n}$ meets the slab $\tau_{n}$ inside $[ig-5\beta,ig+9\beta)$.

For $l=n$ the index $j-i$ is even, and $\bigl(D_{i+2,n}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}$ starts after
$ig+2g-\beta>ig+19\beta-4$, while $\bigl(D_{i-2,n}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}$ ends before
$ig-2g+\beta\le ig-19\beta+4$, hence outside $[ig-5\beta,ig+9\beta)$. Larger even values of $|j-i|$ are even further away, so
only $j=i$ remains. 

For $l=n+1$, at the heights $[\tilde h_{n}+12L,\tilde h_{n}+18L)$ only $B^{+}_{i,n}$
remains, $B^{-,t}_{i,n}$ stopping at $\tilde h_{n}+6L$, and
$\bigl(B^{+}_{i,n}\bigr)_{[\tilde h_{n}+12L,\tilde h_{n}+18L)}
\subseteq[ig+7\beta,ig+15\beta)$. As $D_{j,n+1}$ lies at heights at least
$h_{n+1}=\tilde h_{n}+12L$, these are the only sites of $E^{+}_{i,n}$ it can
meet. The index $j-i$ is odd, and
$\bigl(D_{j,n+1}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}\subseteq(jg-\beta,jg+\beta)$. For $j=i-1$ this ends
before $ig-9\beta+2$ and for $j=i+3$ it starts after $ig+29\beta-6$, both
disjoint from $[ig+7\beta,ig+15\beta)$. Larger odd values of $|j-i|$ are further away, so only $j=i+1$
remains.

\emph{Point (iii).}
$\widehat{E}^{\cdot}_{i,n}$ is contained in the slabs
$\tau_{n-1}+1,\dots,\tau_{n+1}$, so two such sets with $|n-l|\ge2$ occupy
disjoint sets of slabs. For the $x$-coordinates,
$\bigl(B^{+}_{i,n}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}\subseteq[ig-5\beta,ig+15\beta)$ and
$\bigl(B^{-}_{i,n}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}\subseteq(ig-15\beta,ig+5\beta)$, while the
corridors involved are $D_{i,n}$, lying in $(ig-\beta,ig+\beta)$, and, according
to the direction, $D_{i+1,n+1}$ or $D_{i-1,n+1}$, lying in $(ig-11\beta,ig+11\beta)$ since
$g\le10\beta$. Therefore
$\bigl(\widehat{E}^{\cdot}_{i,n}\bigr)_{\mathbb{Z}}\subseteq(ig-15\beta,ig+15\beta)$, an
interval of width $30\beta$. Since $4g>40\beta-8>30\beta$, two such sets with
$|i-j|\ge4$ are disjoint.

title: Proof
body_md:
The event $\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(z))$ is an intersection of crossing
events, thus it is increasing in the occupation configuration. By
\eqref{eq:sandwich} we have $\eta^{\mathrm{crit}}\le\eta^{\xi}$ for every
environment $\xi$, so that, as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018quenched},
\[
  \mathbb{P}^{\xi}\bigl(\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(z))\bigr)
  \ \ge\ \mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(z))\bigr) .
\]
It remains to bound the right-hand side; by the convention of Section~\ref{sec:geometry}, we take $z=0$.

If $k=1$, then by~\eqref{eq:lad3} we have $\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{3}(0))=C^{\uparrow}(R((w,0),(0,18L)))$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018} gives
$\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}(\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{3}(0)))\ge\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon^{N-1}$,
since $\varepsilon\le1$.

Assume $k\ge2$. By~\eqref{eq:lad}, $\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(0))$ is the
intersection of the $k$ increasing events $C^{\uparrow}(T_{j})$ and of the $k-1$
increasing events $C^{\rightarrow}(W_{j})$ or $C^{\leftarrow}(W_{j})$. These
events are not independent, the rails and the rungs overlapping at their ends,
but the Harris--FKG inequality~\cite{Harris1960,FortuinKasteleynGinibre1971}
applies to them under the
product measure $\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}$ and gives
\[
  \mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(0))\bigr)
    \ \ge\ \prod_{0\le j\le k-1}\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(C^{\uparrow}(T_{j})\bigr)
  \prod_{\substack{0\le j\le k-2\\ j\ \text{even}}}\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(C^{\rightarrow}(W_{j})\bigr)
  \prod_{\substack{0\le j\le k-2\\ j\ \text{odd}}}\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}\bigl(C^{\leftarrow}(W_{j})\bigr).
\]
By~\eqref{eq:Tj} each $T_{j}$ is a translate of $R((w,0),(0,18L))$ and by
\eqref{eq:Wj} each $W_{j}$ is a translate of $R((3w,0),(0,6L))$, so each of these
$2k-1$ factors is at least $\varepsilon$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:DuminilCopinTassionTeixeira2018}. Hence
$\mathbb{P}_{p_{c}}(\mathrm{Lad}(\Lambda_{N}(0)))\ge\varepsilon^{2k-1}\ge\varepsilon^{N-1}$,
since $2k-1\le N-1$ and $\varepsilon\le1$.

body_md:
Fix $L$ and $(X_{k})_{k\ge0}$ as given by Proposition~\ref{prop:renormperc}. On
the event that there is an infinite open path of $\mathbb{V}$ starting at
$(0,0)$, Proposition~\ref{prop:reconstruction} gives an infinite open path of
$\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}$, so that
\[
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(\text{there is an infinite open path in }\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}\bigr)\ >\ 0.
\]
The starting point of that path is random, whereas $\Theta$ concerns the origin.
But the event that some infinite open path exists is contained in the countable
union, over $z\in\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}_{+}$, of the events $\{C_{z}\text{ is infinite}\}$, so one of
them has positive probability. The environment is stationary and the uniform
variables are i.i.d., thus translating $z$ to the origin gives
$\Theta(p_{G},p_{c},\delta)=\mathbb{P}(C_{0}\text{ is infinite})>0$.
